extra/supervisor_team.txt.title: Specialist agents
note: **Two full agents, each with a small toolset and a narrow job.**
- The researcher can only look things up; the analyst can only calculate
- Small jobs keep each agent easier to test and less confused

extra/supervisor_team.txt.title: Delegation tools
note: **Each tool runs a whole specialist agent and returns its final answer.**
- This is the supervisor pattern: agents wrapped as tools
- The supervisor can't tell a teammate from a plain tool

extra/supervisor_team.txt.title: The supervisor agent
note: **Coordinates the team - its only tools are the two delegation tools.**
- It plans and routes; it never touches lookup_company or calculate
- The prompt sets the order: facts first, then the math

extra/content_crew.txt.title: Company Analyst agent
note: **A CrewAI agent: role, goal, and backstory, plus the tools it may use.**
- Which tools it calls, and how often, is the agent's choice
- {request} is filled in when the crew starts

extra/content_crew.txt.title: Business Writer agent
note: **The second agent: it writes, after checking the house style guide.**
- Its only tool is get_style_guide

extra/content_crew.txt.title: Analysis task
note: **What the analyst is asked to produce.**
- expected_output tells the agent what 'done' looks like

extra/content_crew.txt.title: Writing task and handoff
note: **context=[analysis_task] pipes the analyst's findings into the writer's prompt.**
- That's the handoff between the two agents

extra/content_crew.txt.title: The crew
note: **Puts agents and tasks together; Process.sequential runs the tasks in list order.**
- The order is fixed - the agentic part is each agent's tool choices

extra/analyst_executor.txt.anchor: # 2. Tell the client we've started (task state: WORKING)
extra/analyst_executor.txt.title: Report WORKING
note: **The task's first status update: the client learns work has started.**

extra/analyst_executor.txt.anchor: # 3. Run the agent step by step
extra/analyst_executor.txt.title: Stream the agent's steps
note: **Runs the agent step by step, sending a WORKING update for every tool it calls.**
- astream hands back each step as the agent works
- An error ends the task as FAILED - a state, not a crash

extra/analyst_executor.txt.anchor: # 4. Publish the answer as an artifact
extra/analyst_executor.txt.title: Deliver the result
note: **The answer becomes an artifact, then the task is marked COMPLETED.**
- You'll watch these events stream live in Lab 4

extra/analyst_server.txt.title: The agent's skill
note: **Describes what this agent can do - other agents read this to decide to use it.**
- Tags and examples help clients (and AI orchestrators) match it

extra/analyst_server.txt.title: The Agent Card
note: **The agent's public contract: name, version, capabilities, skills, and where to reach it.**
- supported_interfaces says 'JSON-RPC at port 9999'
- protocol_version 1.0 must match the A2A-Version header

extra/analyst_server.txt.title: Server wiring
note: **The SDK's request handler plus two sets of routes: the card, and the JSON-RPC methods.**
- InMemoryTaskStore is why GetTask still works after a task finishes

extra/analyst_client.txt.title: 1. Discover
note: **Fetches the Agent Card from the well-known URL - the same JSON you curled in Lab 3.**

extra/analyst_client.txt.title: 2. Connect
note: **Builds a client from the card; the SDK picks the transport the card lists.**
- Our code never mentions JSON-RPC

extra/analyst_client.txt.title: 3. Send and stream
note: **Sends the question and prints each event as it arrives.**
- Status updates carry the agent's progress messages
- streaming=True is what makes them arrive live (step 9)

extra/analyst_client.txt.title: 4. Retrieve
note: **Fetches the finished task by id - anything holding the id can do this later.**

extra/orchestrator.txt.title: Step 1: discover
note: **Fetches every agent's card from its well-known URL.**
- In production this list could come from a registry

extra/orchestrator.txt.title: Step 2: cards become tools
note: **Turns each skill on each card into a tool the model can choose.**
- The description comes straight from the card - that's how the model 'reads' it
- owners remembers which card to call for each tool

extra/orchestrator.txt.title: Step 3: delegate
note: **Sends a task to the chosen agent over A2A and collects its answer.**
- The same client calls you wrote in Lab 4
